Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** that representing aspects of the world through data is necessarily reductive and incomplete. Developer perspective shapes the choice and design of variables
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: Identify variables in datasets that emphasize a particular perspective and the possible impacts of redesigning those datasets
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** different sources of bias in algorithmic and AI systems (societal vs. dataset vs. system parameters) and their interactions
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** and **Understand** metrics to mathematically interpret fairness
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of approaches** for bias mitigation
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** and **Understand** different concepts of justice as they relate to automated decision-making systems
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** context-specific limitations of automated decision-making and **Analyze** when the use of such systems is appropriate and when human decision-making is preferable or required
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** and **Analyze** different standards for interpreting algorithmic and AI decisions: e.g., transparency, explainability
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** different methods and strategies for AI governance
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description:
**Understand** the distinct mechanisms by which AI systems can produce harm
- **Understand** how the unpredictability of generative AI systems and the contexts in which they are deployed means that they cannot, at present, be designed to reliably avoid harmful outcomes
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** strategies to identify, evaluate, and mitigate harms stemming from unpredictability in AI systems
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** the effects of widespread use of synthetic content on one’s ability to control their likeness and public perception
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description:
**Be aware of** the legal frameworks governing copyright and intellectual property as they relate to generative AI
- **Be aware of** questions about whether AI-generated outputs are copyrightable
- **Be aware of** questions regarding the legality of training models on copyrighted data
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** opportunities and risks of generative AI in future of work (e.g., deskilling, lack of connectivity).
Curriculum Objectives.Category: I. Data Science and Artificial Intelligence

Curriculum Objectives.Description:
**Be aware of** the extent of data collection and reliance of technologies on large volumes of personal data
**Understand** the concept of surveillance capitalism and alternative data-driven economic models
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** and **Identify** different mechanisms of data collection—overt, covert, and from other sources (i.e. via sharing)—and their implications on privacy
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** the limitation of the distinction between sensitive and non-sensitive data, especially considering the potential for re-identification
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** the value and functions of privacy (including short-term and long-term privacy threats)
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** (and **Implement**) key aspects of major privacy regulations, standards, etc. (e.g., CCPA, GDPR, …)
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Analyze** trade-offs between privacy and other values, such as transparency, accountability, safety, or security
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** surveillance and **Identify** instances of data collection that enable surveillance
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** different conceptions of consent, their potential, and limitations, as an instrument for data protection
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description:
**Be aware of** widely-used privacy-preserving/enhancing technologies (e.g., encryption, differential privacy)
- **Understand** their limitations
- **Analyze** prominent controversies surrounding them
Curriculum Objectives.Category: II. Data Collection, Protection, and Privacy

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** (and **Implement**) different design processes for evaluating the needs of diverse users and **Analyze** their appropriateness in various contexts
**Understand** and **Identify** how different biases can influence one’s judgment and shape design decisions
**Understand** varying definitions and conceptions of accessibility
**Identify** opportunities to apply and Implement standards and best practices for accessibility
**Identify** and **Analyze** intersections between accessibility and other values such as privacy, security, or sustainability
**Be aware of** how technology is used to direct users’ attention and shape their interests, preferences, and desires
**Be aware of** the psychological mechanisms and cognitive biases which are exploited in directing user attention (e.g., nudging) and their technical implementations
**Analyze** the value of attention and the consequences of yielding control over it
**Analyze** the effect of technologies on our self-perception and relationship with ourselves
**Analyze** the effect of technologies on the nature and quality of interpersonal relationships

**Be aware of** and **Identify** potential environmental impacts of a specific technology: 
- Natural resource consumption
- Energy consumption
- E-waste production
- Pollution
**Understand** how the environmental impacts of technology have disproportionate socio-economic effects on different populations

**Understand** the need for infrastructural sustainability and the means and challenges of ensuring hardware and software maintenance and preservation
- **Analyze** software preservation efforts in the context of broader perspectives on preservation (e.g., of cultural heritage)
**Understand** the need for and challenges of ensuring data sustainability

**Identify** skills and roles that advancements in specific technologies (e.g. automation, generative AI)  are likely to displace, create, or evolve, and **Analyze** the (socio-)economic implications of these changes

**Be aware of** the (often exploitative) human labor involved in and the physical and psychological effects of:
- Training AI models (including data labeling and curation)
- Surveillance
- Content Moderation
- Hardware fabrication and resource collection
- Data generation

**Understand** the effect of content moderation on social pluralism 
- **Analyze** the tensions between free expression of ideas and user safety/comfort in online spaces
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.c. The Internet and Public Discourse

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** the effects of algorithmic/AI-based curation of information on public discourse (e.g., filter bubbles, echo chambers)
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.c. The Internet and Public Discourse

Curriculum Objectives.Description:
**Understand** the role of specific technologies (e.g., social media, generative AI) in spreading misinformation or disinformation
- **Be aware of** the effect of specific technologies on erosion of trust in individuals, institutions, and providers of information
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.c. The Internet and Public Discourse

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** the potential and limitations of technical and non-technical mitigation approaches to curb the spread of mis-/disinformation
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.c. The Internet and Public Discourse

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** how technical infrastructure and regulation of that infrastructure shapes the ways in which we communicate and consume information
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.c. The Internet and Public Discourse

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** how sousveillance (watching the watchers), enabled by easy access to recording devices and social networks for distribution, creates transparency and enables individuals and social movements to hold institutions and other powerful actors accountable
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.c. The Internet and Public Discourse

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** the global impacts of technological developments and political and economic power structures that shape them
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.d. Technology, History, and International Relations

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Be aware of** the long-term history of technological development and Analyze the impact of current changes in light of that history
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.d. Technology, History, and International Relations

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Analyze** the impact of technology on military capabilities and conflict
Curriculum Objectives.Subcategory: IV.d. Technology, History, and International Relations

Curriculum Objectives.Description: **Understand** the concept of a stakeholder and Identify various stakeholders in a given project
**Identify** and **Implement** stakeholder needs
**Analyze** how different stakeholders’ needs may conflict and potential resolution strategies
**Understand** how to communicate technical content to non-technical stakeholders
**Analyze** the alignment of a project with stakeholders' intended goals
**Identify** and **Analyze** techno-solutionist attitudes and approaches

**Analyze** the potential impacts of technologies with a broad socio-political view, especially those that are ostensibly designed for social benefit
- **Analyze** conflicting positions on the extent to which stakeholder requests should be implemented, in cases where stakeholder requests may diverge from what might benefit them (i.e. paternalism versus libertarianism)

**Be aware of** responsible disclosure
- **Be aware of** the existence of mechanisms for reporting technological vulnerabilities to responsible organizations
- **Analyze** possible impacts of releasing security vulnerabilities publicly
